subject.title: [Feature]: Add realtime video frame transport for provider and gateway relay sessions

question: Should OpenClaw allow camera-derived frames to transit gateway/provider plugin relay sessions, and if so what narrow SDK/RPC contract and consent/validation rules must gate it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature would create a new sensitive-data transport and public SDK/gateway contract that automation cannot safely choose without maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Approve A Narrow One-Shot Frame Seam
options.body: Define an additive bridge/RPC contract for explicit one-frame submissions with MIME and size validation, consent requirements, redaction/logging rules, provider mappings, docs, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Browser-Direct Only For Now
options.body: Defer gateway/provider relay image transport and limit visual context to the browser-direct PR until maintainers are comfortable with camera data crossing server/plugin boundaries.

options.title: Reject Realtime Frame Transport
options.body: Close the transport direction and steer users to existing static image/video media-understanding flows or future ClawHub/plugin-specific experiments instead.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow One-Shot Frame Seam
recommendation.body: Define an additive bridge/RPC contract for explicit one-frame submissions with MIME and size validation, consent requirements, redaction/logging rules, provider mappings, docs, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is assigned to the issue and has the strongest recent history across Talk provider, Plugin SDK, gateway protocol, and UI Talk surfaces.
